nameStory: The 'squat' in this snail's name comes from its short, stocky shell shape - it's wider than it is tall, giving it a compressed appearance. 'Duskysnail' refers to the typically dark, muted coloration of these tiny freshwater mollusks, which helps them blend into murky pond and stream bottoms.
description: The squat duskysnail is a tiny freshwater snail that you'd need a magnifying glass to properly examine - most are smaller than a peppercorn. It has a low, rounded shell that's wider than it is tall, giving it that characteristic 'squat' appearance. Like other aquatic snails, it breathes through gills and has a small door-like cover called an operculum that can seal its shell opening. These minute mollusks live their entire lives underwater in freshwater habitats.

idTips.label: Shell Shape
idTips.description: Low, rounded shell that's noticeably wider than it is tall, giving it a flattened or compressed look when viewed from the side

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Extremely small - typically smaller than a peppercorn and requiring magnification to see details clearly

idTips.label: Operculum
idTips.description: Possesses a small, hard door-like cover that can completely close off the shell opening when the snail retreats inside

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Shell appears dusky or dark-toned, often brownish or grayish, helping it blend with sediment and debris

idTips.label: Habitat Preference
idTips.description: Always found underwater in freshwater environments, never on land or in saltwater

habitat: Squat duskysnails inhabit freshwater environments including slow-moving streams, ponds, and lake margins where they crawl along the bottom sediment. They prefer areas with soft substrates where they can feed on organic matter and microscopic algae. Look for them in shallow, quiet waters with muddy or silty bottoms, often among aquatic vegetation.

seasonality.spring: Active as waters warm, beginning to reproduce. Best time to search as water levels are often lower and clearer from snowmelt.
seasonality.summer: Most active period with peak reproduction. Easier to spot in warm, shallow waters during calm morning hours.
seasonality.fall: Remain active but may move to slightly deeper waters. Still observable but populations may be more dispersed.
seasonality.winter: Less active in cold water but don't hibernate. May be found in deeper areas or under ice in protected spots.

funFact: Despite being so tiny you need a magnifying glass to see them properly, squat duskysnails are actually complex little machines - they have thousands of microscopic teeth on their tongue-like radula that work like a living file to scrape algae and bacteria off surfaces underwater!
confusionNotes: Most easily confused with other minute freshwater snails, but the distinctly squat, flattened shell shape sets it apart from the more tower-like or rounded shells of similar species. Memory trick: 'squat' means short and wide, just like this snail's shell.
contextualKnowledge: With only 2 recorded observations in New England, this species is either extremely rare in our region or simply overlooked due to its minute size - many amateur naturalists miss these tiny snails entirely because they require magnification to identify properly.
compareHints: Since no other Lyogyrus species are recorded in New England, compare with other small duskysnails in the Amnicolidae family. The squat duskysnail's distinctly flattened, wider-than-tall shell shape distinguishes it from most other minute freshwater snails, which tend to have more elongated or evenly rounded shells.
